Nebo
NEE-boh
proper noun
Hebrew nebo, a name of uncertain meaning, perhaps “height,” here a town of Judah or Benjamin whose men returned from the captivity in Babylon.

📖 Biblical Definition

Nebo, in this place, is the name of a small town whose men, two and fifty of them, are numbered among those who returned from the captivity of Babylon with Zerubbabel (Ezr 2:29; Neh 7:33). It is carefully to be distinguished from Mount Nebo in the land of Moab, that height of Pisgah whither Moses went up to behold the promised land before he died and was buried by the hand of the LORD; and from Nebo the idol of Babylon, that bowed and stooped with Bel when the LORD brought down the gods of the captors. The dictionary marks these apart, that the reader confound not the town of the returnees with the mountain of Moses’ death nor with the heathen god. Of this Nebo the Scripture records only the number of its men in the book of the return, yet that is no small honour, for they were among the remnant whose spirit God had raised to go up and rebuild. The men of Nebo are named again among those who had taken strange wives and put them away in the days of Ezra’s reformation (Ezr 10:43). Nebo stands as a witness that the providence of God numbered even this little company in the great gathering home, and that the LORD, who buries His servant Moses and casts down the idols of Babylon, loses not the least of His returning people.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

A town of Judah or Benjamin whose two and fifty men returned from the captivity in Babylon.

NEBO, a town whose men returned from the captivity in Babylon.

Two and fifty of its men are numbered in the registers of the return.

It is to be distinguished from Mount Nebo, where Moses died, in Moab.

It is also distinct from Nebo the idol of Babylon, named with Bel.

It witnesses to the LORD’s numbering of the least company of His remnant.

📖 Key Scripture

Ezr 2:29 — "The children of Nebo, fifty and two."

Neh 7:33 — "The men of the other Nebo, fifty and two."

Deu 34:1 — "And Moses went up from the plains of Moab unto the mountain of Nebo, to the top of Pisgah, that is over against Jericho. And the LORD shewed him all the land of Gilead, unto Dan,"

Isa 46:1 — "Bel boweth down, Nebo stoopeth, their idols were upon the beasts, and upon the cattle: your carriages were heavy loaden; they are a burden to the weary beast."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

A town of Scripture, not a contested doctrine; it witnesses to the LORD’s numbering of the least company of His remnant.

expand to see more

The town of Nebo is a name of the sacred registers of the return, and no movement of the present age has troubled itself to redefine it. The dictionary records it, and distinguishes it plainly from Mount Nebo where Moses died and from Nebo the idol of Babylon, that the reader who meets the name among the returnees may know it for a real town and a real people brought home by a real God.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the providence of God who numbers the least of His remnant. He who buried His servant Moses upon the height of Nebo, and cast down the idol Nebo that stooped before Him, is the same who counted the two and fifty men of the town of Nebo in the book of the return. The saint of small account may take heart that the LORD who is mighty over kings and idols forgets not the least company of His returning people.
